header:
How Google makes
money from free

lines.text: Google's free. Its ads made over $800 million a day.
lines.say: Google's free. Its ads made over eight hundred million a day.

lines.text: That's 2025: $294.7 billion in ads, or about $807 million a day, by our math.
lines.say: That's twenty twenty-five: two hundred ninety-four point seven billion dollars in ads, or about eight hundred seven million a day, by our math.

lines.text: So how does a company that charges you zero become one of the biggest money machines on Earth?
lines.say: So how does a company that charges you zero become one of the biggest money machines on Earth?

lines.text: Short answer: you're not the customer. You're the reason the customer shows up.
lines.say: Short answer: you're not the customer. You're the reason the customer shows up.

lines.text: In this video: the auction behind every search, the bill for being the default, the court case, and what comes after ads.
lines.say: In this video: the auction behind every search, the bill for being the default, the court case, and what comes after ads.

lines.text: Every number comes from Alphabet's filings, with dates attached. This is education, not advice about any stock.

lines.text: Chapter 1: The free trick
lines.say: Chapter one: the free trick.

lines.text: Google started in 1998 as a search engine with no real way to make money.
lines.say: Google started in nineteen ninety-eight as a search engine with no real way to make money.

lines.text: The fix came in 2000, with a product called AdWords: small text ads next to your results.
lines.say: The fix came in two thousand, with a product called AdWords: small text ads next to your results.

lines.text: By 2004 that ad engine was big enough to take Google public.
lines.say: By two thousand four that ad engine was big enough to take Google public.

lines.text: In 2006 it bought YouTube, which turned free videos into another giant ad shelf.
lines.say: In two thousand six it bought YouTube, which turned free videos into another giant ad shelf.

lines.text: And in 2015 it reorganized under a parent company called Alphabet. Google is still where nearly all the money comes from.
lines.say: And in twenty fifteen it reorganized under a parent company called Alphabet. Google is still where nearly all the money comes from.

lines.text: Here's the trick. When you type a search, you tell Google exactly what you want, right now.
lines.say: Here's the trick. When you type a search, you tell Google exactly what you want, right now.

lines.text: A TV ad guesses who's watching. A search ad knows. Someone typing 'plumber near me' isn't browsing. They're buying.
lines.say: A TV ad guesses who's watching. A search ad knows. Someone typing 'plumber near me' isn't browsing. They're buying.

lines.text: That moment of intent is the product. Google sells a spot in front of it.
lines.say: That moment of intent is the product. Google sells a spot in front of it.

lines.text: And it doesn't set the price. Advertisers set it, in an auction that runs in a split second every time you search.
lines.say: And it doesn't set the price. Advertisers set it, in an auction that runs in a split second every time you search.

lines.text: Chapter 2: Inside the ad auction
lines.say: Chapter two: inside the ad auction.

lines.text: Advertisers pick keywords and a maximum bid: the most they'll pay for one click.
lines.say: Advertisers pick keywords and a maximum bid: the most they'll pay for one click.

lines.text: That's the core idea: cost per click. A business pays nothing when you see its ad, only when you click it.
lines.say: That's the core idea: cost per click. A business pays nothing when you see its ad, only when you click it.

lines.text: But the highest bid doesn't automatically win. Google also grades each ad.
lines.say: But the highest bid doesn't automatically win. Google also grades each ad.

lines.text: That grade is Quality Score, a 1 to 10 rating for each keyword.
lines.say: That grade is Quality Score, a one to ten rating for each keyword.

lines.text: It looks at three things. First, how likely people are to click the ad.
lines.say: It looks at three things. First, how likely people are to click the ad.

lines.text: Second, how well the ad matches what you searched.
lines.say: Second, how well the ad matches what you searched.

lines.text: Third, how good the page is after you click.
lines.say: Third, how good the page is after you click.

lines.text: Google doesn't publish its exact formula. But marketers use a simple version: bid times Quality Score equals Ad Rank.
lines.say: Google doesn't publish its exact formula. But marketers use a simple version: bid times Quality Score equals Ad Rank.

lines.text: Let's run it. This is a simplified example, our math.
lines.say: Let's run it. This is a simplified example, our math.

lines.text: Ann bids $4 a click, but her ad is so-so: Quality Score 5. Her Ad Rank is 20.
lines.say: Ann bids four dollars a click, but her ad is so-so: Quality Score five. Her Ad Rank is twenty.

lines.text: Ben bids only $3, but his ad is great: Quality Score 8. His Ad Rank is 24. Ben wins the top spot.
lines.say: Ben bids only three dollars, but his ad is great: Quality Score eight. His Ad Rank is twenty-four. Ben wins the top spot.

lines.text: And Ben doesn't pay his full $3. He pays just enough to beat Ann: 20 divided by 8, plus a penny. That's $2.51.
lines.say: And Ben doesn't pay his full three dollars. He pays just enough to beat Ann: twenty divided by eight, plus a penny. That's two dollars and fifty-one cents.

lines.text: That's the clever part. Better ads pay less, so users see more useful ads and keep searching.
lines.say: That's the clever part. Better ads pay less, so users see more useful ads and keep searching.

lines.text: Now multiply that by billions of searches. In 2025, Alphabet said paid clicks rose 6% and the average cost per click rose 7%.
lines.say: Now multiply that by billions of searches. In twenty twenty-five, Alphabet said paid clicks rose six percent and the average cost per click rose seven percent.

lines.text: More clicks, and each one a bit pricier. That combo is the engine.
lines.say: More clicks, and each one a bit pricier. That combo is the engine.

lines.text: And the auction starts fresh on the very next search, with new bidders and new prices, all day, every day.
lines.say: And the auction starts fresh on the very next search, with new bidders and new prices, all day, every day.

lines.text: Chapter 3: The money machine
lines.say: Chapter three: the money machine.

lines.text: Here's Alphabet's total revenue from 2015 to 2025, straight from its annual reports.
lines.say: Here's Alphabet's total revenue from twenty fifteen to twenty twenty-five, straight from its annual reports.

lines.text: In 2015 it was about $75 billion. In 2025 it hit $402.8 billion, the first year above $400 billion.
lines.say: In twenty fifteen it was about seventy-five billion dollars. In twenty twenty-five it hit four hundred two point eight billion, the first year above four hundred billion.

lines.text: Look at 2021. Revenue jumped from $182.5 billion to $257.6 billion, up 41% in a year, as ad spending boomed online.
lines.say: Look at twenty twenty-one. Revenue jumped from one hundred eighty-two point five billion to two hundred fifty-seven point six billion, up forty-one percent in a year, as ad spending boomed online.

lines.text: From 2015 to 2025, revenue grew about 5.4 times, by our math.
lines.say: From twenty fifteen to twenty twenty-five, revenue grew about five point four times, by our math.

lines.text: So where did the 2025 money come from? Mostly from three ad shelves.
lines.say: So where did the twenty twenty-five money come from? Mostly from three ad shelves.

lines.text: Search and other brought in $224.5 billion. That's the ads around your search results, Maps and more.
lines.say: Search and other brought in two hundred twenty-four point five billion dollars. That's the ads around your search results, Maps and more.

lines.text: YouTube ads added $40.4 billion.
lines.say: YouTube ads added forty point four billion.

lines.text: And the Network, ads Google places on other people's websites and apps, made $29.8 billion.
lines.say: And the Network, ads Google places on other people's websites and apps, made twenty-nine point eight billion.

lines.text: Network actually slipped in 2025, from $30.4 billion the year before, on lower AdSense revenue, Alphabet said.
lines.say: Network actually slipped in twenty twenty-five, from thirty point four billion the year before, on lower AdSense revenue, Alphabet said.

lines.text: YouTube is bigger than its ad line, though. Counting ads and subscriptions, it brought in over $60 billion in 2025, Alphabet said.
lines.say: YouTube is bigger than its ad line, though. Counting ads and subscriptions, it brought in over sixty billion dollars in twenty twenty-five, Alphabet said.

lines.text: Add them up and ads were $294.7 billion, about 73% of all revenue in 2025, by our math.
lines.say: Add them up and ads were two hundred ninety-four point seven billion dollars, about seventy-three percent of all revenue in twenty twenty-five, by our math.

lines.text: Now break that ad money down to time. $294.7 billion over 365 days is about $807 million a day.
lines.say: Now break that ad money down to time. Two hundred ninety-four point seven billion over three hundred sixty-five days is about eight hundred seven million a day.

lines.text: That's about $33.6 million an hour, or roughly $9,345 every second, by our math.
lines.say: That's about thirty-three point six million dollars an hour, or roughly nine thousand three hundred forty-five dollars every second, by our math.

lines.text: By the time you finish one search, Google's ads have made thousands of dollars.
lines.say: By the time you finish one search, Google's ads have made thousands of dollars.

lines.text: Chapter 4: Paying for the front door
lines.say: Chapter four: paying for the front door.

lines.text: Here's the part most people never hear about. Google pays a fortune to be the place you search.
lines.say: Here's the part most people never hear about. Google pays a fortune to be the place you search.

lines.text: Those payments are called traffic acquisition costs, or TAC.
lines.say: Those payments are called traffic acquisition costs, or T A C.

lines.text: Some goes to websites that show Google's ads. A lot goes to browsers, phone makers and carriers that make Google the default.
lines.say: Some goes to websites that show Google's ads. A lot goes to browsers, phone makers and carriers that make Google the default.

lines.text: In the July to September 2026 quarter, Google ads brought in $82.0 billion.
lines.say: In the July to September twenty twenty-six quarter, Google ads brought in eighty-two billion dollars.

lines.text: And $16.4 billion went back out to partners. That's 20% of ad revenue, or $1 of every $5.
lines.say: And sixteen point four billion went back out to partners. That's twenty percent of ad revenue, or one dollar of every five.

lines.text: The biggest single check goes to Apple.
lines.say: The biggest single check goes to Apple.

lines.text: Court documents unsealed in 2024 showed Google paid Apple $20 billion in 2022 to be Safari's default search engine.
lines.say: Court documents unsealed in twenty twenty-four showed Google paid Apple twenty billion dollars in twenty twenty-two to be Safari's default search engine.

lines.text: A Google expert witness also testified in 2023 that Google shares 36% of its Safari search ad revenue with Apple.
lines.say: A Google expert witness also testified in twenty twenty-three that Google shares thirty-six percent of its Safari search ad revenue with Apple.

lines.text: Why pay that much? Because most people never change the default. Being first in line is worth billions.
lines.say: Why pay that much? Because most people never change the default. Being first in line is worth billions.

lines.text: For Google, the math works: the searches are worth more than the check. But that same check put it in court.
lines.say: For Google, the math works: the searches are worth more than the check. But that same check put it in court.

lines.text: Chapter 5: The court case
lines.say: Chapter five: the court case.

lines.text: The US Justice Department sued Google in 2020, arguing deals like the Apple one shut out rival search engines.
lines.say: The US Justice Department sued Google in twenty twenty, arguing deals like the Apple one shut out rival search engines.

lines.text: In August 2024, Judge Amit Mehta ruled that Google illegally kept a monopoly in search.
lines.say: In August twenty twenty-four, Judge Amit Mehta ruled that Google illegally kept a monopoly in search.

lines.text: His words were blunt.
lines.say: His words were blunt.

scene.text: Google is a monopolist, and it has acted as one to maintain its monopoly.

lines.text: In September 2025 came the remedies. Google was not forced to sell Chrome or Android.
lines.say: In September twenty twenty-five came the remedies. Google was not forced to sell Chrome or Android.

lines.text: But it can no longer sign exclusive deals for Search, Chrome, Assistant or Gemini.
lines.say: But it can no longer sign exclusive deals for Search, Chrome, Assistant or Gemini.

lines.text: It can still pay partners like Apple for placement, just not to lock rivals out.
lines.say: It can still pay partners like Apple for placement, just not to lock rivals out.

lines.text: And it must share some search index and user data with qualified competitors.
lines.say: And it must share some search index and user data with qualified competitors.

lines.text: The idea behind the data sharing is to help rival search engines catch up, under a court-appointed technical committee's watch.
lines.say: The idea behind the data sharing is to help rival search engines catch up, under a court-appointed technical committee's watch.

lines.text: Google appealed in January 2026, challenging the ruling itself.
lines.say: Google appealed in January twenty twenty-six, challenging the ruling itself.

lines.text: The Justice Department and states cross-appealed in February 2026, asking for tougher remedies. As of November 2026, the appeals court hadn't ruled.
lines.say: The Justice Department and states cross-appealed in February twenty twenty-six, asking for tougher remedies. As of November twenty twenty-six, the appeals court hadn't ruled.

lines.text: The Justice Department says rivals need more room. Google says the rules hurt users. We'll leave that to the courts.
lines.say: The Justice Department says rivals need more room. Google says the rules hurt users. We'll leave that to the courts.

lines.text: Chapter 6: Beyond the ads
lines.say: Chapter six: beyond the ads.

lines.text: Ads still dominate, but Google has been building money machines that don't depend on them.
lines.say: Ads still dominate, but Google has been building money machines that don't depend on them.

lines.text: In 2025, Google Cloud, which rents computing power and AI tools to businesses, made about $58.7 billion.
lines.say: In twenty twenty-five, Google Cloud, which rents computing power and AI tools to businesses, made about fifty-eight point seven billion dollars.

lines.text: Subscriptions, platforms and devices, think YouTube Premium, Google One storage, app store fees and Pixel phones, made about $48 billion.
lines.say: Subscriptions, platforms and devices, think YouTube Premium, Google One storage, app store fees and Pixel phones, made about forty-eight billion.

lines.text: Then came the July to September 2026 quarter, reported in late October. Total revenue was $127.6 billion, up 25%.
lines.say: Then came the July to September twenty twenty-six quarter, reported in late October. Total revenue was one hundred twenty-seven point six billion dollars, up twenty-five percent.

lines.text: Search still grew 12%, to $63.35 billion. YouTube ads grew about 9%, to $11.2 billion.
lines.say: Search still grew twelve percent, to sixty-three point three five billion. YouTube ads grew about nine percent, to eleven point two billion.

lines.text: But the jaw-dropper was Cloud: $30.7 billion, up from $15.2 billion a year earlier.
lines.say: But the jaw-dropper was Cloud: thirty point seven billion, up from fifteen point two billion a year earlier.

lines.text: That's 103% growth in a single year, as companies rushed to rent AI computing.
lines.say: That's one hundred three percent growth in a single year, as companies rushed to rent AI computing.

lines.text: It got more profitable too. Cloud's operating margin was 36.2% in that quarter, up from 23.7% a year earlier.
lines.say: It got more profitable too. Cloud's operating margin was thirty-six point two percent in that quarter, up from twenty-three point seven percent a year earlier.

lines.text: Because of that, ads were about 64% of revenue in that quarter, down from about 73% in 2025, by our math.
lines.say: Because of that, ads were about sixty-four percent of revenue in that quarter, down from about seventy-three percent in twenty twenty-five, by our math.

lines.text: And AI is changing search itself. Alphabet said in July 2025 that AI Overviews had over 2 billion monthly users.
lines.say: And AI is changing search itself. Alphabet said in July twenty twenty-five that AI Overviews had over two billion monthly users.

lines.text: The open question: if an AI answers you directly, do you still click an ad? Google is now putting ads inside AI answers too.
lines.say: The open question: if an AI answers you directly, do you still click an ad? Google is now putting ads inside AI answers too.

lines.text: That's the big risk. The auction only pays when people click, and AI could change how often they do.
lines.say: That's the big risk. The auction only pays when people click, and AI could change how often they do.

lines.text: Chapter 7: What it means for you
lines.say: Chapter seven: what it means for you.

lines.text: First: free has a price. You pay with your attention and your data, and that's what advertisers buy.
lines.say: First: free has a price. You pay with your attention and your data, and that's what advertisers buy.

lines.text: Second: the top results are often ads. Look for the small 'Sponsored' label before you click.
lines.say: Second: the top results are often ads. Look for the small 'Sponsored' label before you click.

lines.text: Third: every click a business pays for gets built into its prices. Those ad costs don't vanish. Customers cover them.
lines.say: Third: every click a business pays for gets built into its prices. Those ad costs don't vanish. Customers cover them.

lines.text: And fourth: defaults are powerful. You can change your search engine in a few taps. Google paid Apple $20 billion in 2022 betting you won't.
lines.say: And fourth: defaults are powerful. You can change your search engine in a few taps. Google paid Apple twenty billion dollars in twenty twenty-two betting you won't.

lines.text: None of this says whether the stock is a good or bad idea. It's just how the machine works.
lines.say: None of this says whether the stock is a good or bad idea. It's just how the machine works.

lines.text: So let's recap how Google makes money from free.
lines.say: So let's recap how Google makes money from free.

lines.text: It gives you search and video for free and sells your attention to advertisers.
lines.say: It gives you search and video for free and sells your attention to advertisers.

lines.text: It prices that attention with a split-second auction, where better ads pay less per click.
lines.say: It prices that attention with a split-second auction, where better ads pay less per click.

lines.text: It pays partners like Apple billions to be the front door, a deal the courts are still weighing.
lines.say: It pays partners like Apple billions to be the front door, a deal the courts are still weighing.

lines.text: And it's growing Cloud fast, so ads were a smaller share of revenue by the third quarter of 2026.
lines.say: And it's growing Cloud fast, so ads were a smaller share of revenue by the third quarter of twenty twenty-six.

lines.text: In 2025, that added up to over $800 million a day from ads, from a product you never paid a cent for.
lines.say: In twenty twenty-five, that added up to over eight hundred million dollars a day from ads, from a product you never paid a cent for.

lines.text: Next time you search, remember: there's an auction happening behind it, and you're what's being bid on.
lines.say: Next time you search, remember: there's an auction happening behind it, and you're what's being bid on.

post.title: Google Is Free. Its Ads Made $800M+ a Day in 2025.
post.ig: You pay Google nothing, yet its ads made over $800 million a day in 2025. Here's the auction behind every search.
post.tiktok: Google is free, yet its ads made over $800M a day in 2025. The auction, the Apple deal and the court case, explained.
post.yt_desc:
Google charges you nothing, yet in 2025 Alphabet's ads brought in $294.7 billion, about $807 million a day by our math. This video explains how the search ad auction works (cost per click, Quality Score and a worked example), why Google paid Apple $20 billion in 2022 to be Safari's default, and what the 2024 antitrust ruling and 2025 remedies did. We chart Alphabet's revenue from 2015 to 2025 and look at its July-September 2026 quarter, when Google Cloud revenue more than doubled to $30.7 billion.

News and education, not financial advice.
